ns2:section.sectionText: Polymer Rheology Course builds a molecular understanding of polymer characterization and properties and develops a link between the physical chemistry of the microstructure and the macroscopic behaviors. The course begins with polymeric descriptions from a physical basis and continues with polymer solution thermodynamics in the context of Flory-Huggins theory. After fundamentals, the course considers polymer characterization from a rheological (flow and deformation) perspective with overage of dynamics, linear and nonlinear viscoelasticity, the rheology of dilute and networked polymer systems, and time-temperature superposition. The course concludes with models for dilute polymeric suspensions, unentangled polymer melts, entanglements, and the reptation model. Meets with CHBE 594 SAR.
